recent_posts.title: Debugging pthread condition variable timeouts with CLOCK_REALTIME and spurious wakeups
recent_posts.summary: A developer debugs intermittent test failures caused by POSIX condition variable timeouts returning too early. The root cause was twofold: using CLOCK_REALTIME for absolute timeouts while NTP was adjusting system time backwards, and not handling spurious wakeups from pthread_cond_timedwait(). Switching to CLOCK_MONOTONIC and adding spurious wakeup handling resolved the issue. The investigation highlights why CLOCK_REALTIME shouldn't be used for measuring delays and why POSIX timed operations require explicit timeout management.

recent_posts.title: Compiler Versioning and Continuous Integration
recent_posts.summary: A detailed guide on managing multiple Visual Studio compiler versions for continuous integration builds. The approach involves exporting Visual Studio configurations as vsconfig files, installing custom toolchain versions in separate directories, and configuring CI systems to use specific compiler versions for different code releases. This prevents build failures when older code becomes incompatible with newer compiler versions, ensuring reproducible builds across different project versions.

recent_posts.title: AFD datagram performance
recent_posts.summary: Experimentation with the Windows networking stack's `\Device\Afd` readiness interface has shown performance benefits over traditional IOCP designs. Specifically, using a single well-known socket and processing datagrams in sequence can reduce CPU usage, improve round trip times, and support more concurrent connections under heavy server loads. The AFD design is efficient for both reading and sending data, minimizing context switches and user-to-kernel transitions.

recent_posts.summary: The author discusses a challenge encountered while optimizing a continuous integration build system for a cloud gaming client's server, specifically dealing with project GUID mismatches in Visual Studio. To improve build times, they consolidated separate project builds into a single solution build followed by isolated project builds. They also highlight the importance of unique project GUIDs within Visual Studio solutions to avoid build errors.

recent_posts.title: A multi-connection AFD-based echo server
recent_posts.summary: The author discusses the implementation of a multi-connection echo server using individual socket polling with AFD. They compare this approach to an earlier set-based method, highlighting the scalability benefits of individual polling. The new method reduces complexity and uses the IOCP for handling completions efficiently. Important details such as the use of the `Exclusive` flag and associating sockets with IOCP are elaborated upon. Performance considerations between independent polling and set polling are also discussed.

recent_posts.title: Socket readiness without \Device\Afd
recent_posts.summary: Learn about an alternative approach to socket readiness notifications on Windows using c-ares and avoiding the use of the \Device\Afd interface. Polling each socket separately can provide a powerful design choice.
